eval_dimensions.name: Notification Transport Resolution
eval_dimensions.description: Step 3 resolves Slack vs Google Chat from whichever per-repo config names the repo, runs both when both do, and asks when neither does (GH-1308)

eval_dimensions.name: Approval State Precheck
eval_dimensions.description: Step 1.5 filters bot approvals before matching reviews against headRefOid, and gates on a human approval of the current HEAD

eval_dimensions.name: Readiness Gate
eval_dimensions.description: Step 1.6 refuses (unattended) or asks (attended) before any reviewer is pinged when CI is not green, review threads are open, a blocking bot is not at head, or the PR is a draft (GH-1834)

eval_dimensions.name: Readiness Audit
eval_dimensions.description: --audit classifies review-requested PRs as SENT-NOT-READY or WENT-RED-AFTER through review_readiness_audit and writes nothing (GH-1834)

eval_dimensions.name: Skill Delegation
eval_dimensions.description: Assignment and notification are delegated to the sibling skills, never inlined as raw gh or API calls

evals.name: chat-only-repo-reaches-its-transport
evals.description: GH-1308: the repo is named only in the Google Chat config. Before the fix, Step 3 was hardcoded to Slack and a Chat-only team had no supported path through this skill — the observed session passed the transport as a free-text argument and the agent substituted the sibling skill on its own.

assertions.text: Delegates to dev10x:gchat-review-request, the transport whose config names the repo
Does NOT invoke the Slack sibling — its config does not name this repo
Step 4 summary reports Google Chat rather than a hardcoded 'Slack notification' line

evals.name: both-configs-name-the-repo
evals.description: Mirroring review requests into Slack and Chat is a legitimate configuration, so Step 3 must not assume exactly one transport.

assertions.text: Invokes both sibling skills rather than picking one

evals.name: no-config-fires-the-transport-gate
evals.description: Neither config names the repo. The skill must ask where the request should go rather than failing into silence or guessing a transport.

assertions.text: Fires AskUserQuestion — a plain-text question would let the skill auto-proceed without an answer
The widget offers Slack, Google Chat, and Skip the notification
Neither sibling skill is invoked before the user answers

evals.name: bot-approval-does-not-short-circuit
evals.description: GH-128: only a bot has approved the current HEAD. A bot approval must not satisfy the human-review requirement, so the skill proceeds to request review rather than offering to merge.

assertions.text: Continues to Step 2 instead of firing the skip-and-merge gate

evals.name: human-approval-on-head-fires-the-merge-gate
evals.description: A human has approved the current HEAD, so pinging reviewers again is noise. The skill must ask rather than silently short-circuiting.

assertions.text: Fires AskUserQuestion with Skip / Force request / Cancel

evals.name: red-ci-attended-fires-the-readiness-gate
evals.description: GH-1834: CI is failing on the head. A reviewer must not be pinged on a PR that was never ready, so the attended run asks before Step 2, with stopping recommended.

assertions.text: Fires AskUserQuestion rather than a plain-text question
No inline plain-text 'request review anyway?' question substitutes for, or precedes, the widget
signals: No inline 'Request review anyway?' before the AskUserQuestion call

assertions.text: The widget leads with 'Stop — fix it first (Recommended)' and offers 'Request review anyway'
dev10x:gh-pr-request-review is not invoked before the user answers

evals.name: unattended-refuses-unresolved-threads
evals.description: GH-1834: two review threads are still open. Unattended callers have nobody to ask, so the skill refuses: no reviewer, no chat post, no PR comment.

assertions.text: Does NOT invoke dev10x:gh-pr-request-review
Does NOT invoke either chat transport
Reports the open threads as the reason for refusing

evals.name: unattended-refuses-a-draft-without-publishing-it
evals.description: GH-1834: the PR is still a draft. A draft is a failing condition like red CI. Marking it ready inside the check would publish the PR and notify code owners even on a refusal, so the unattended run refuses and leaves the draft alone.

assertions.text: Does NOT call pr_ready — the check never publishes a draft
Does NOT invoke dev10x:gh-pr-request-review
Reports the draft as the reason for refusing

evals.name: audit-mode-classifies-and-writes-nothing
evals.description: GH-1834: the audit looks back at PRs already sent and tells the requester's misses (SENT-NOT-READY) from later breakage (WENT-RED-AFTER). It is read-only.

assertions.text: Calls review_readiness_audit
Does NOT request review or post a notification
Groups the output by verdict

evals.name: child-stop-ends-the-run
evals.description: GH-1834: the PR was a draft; the user answered 'Request review anyway' in Step 1.6. gh-pr-request-review flipped it, CI went red, the user chose 'Stop — fix it first', and the child returned it to draft, ending its output with 'Readiness: stopped — …'. Nobody was asked to review, so no chat notification or PR comment may go out.

assertions.text: Step 2 invokes dev10x:gh-pr-request-review, so the stop path is reached
Does NOT post a chat notification or a PR comment
The summary repeats the sibling's stop line

evals.name: plan-step-call-refuses-with-stop-marker
evals.prompt: Skill(skill="dev10x:request-review", args="--pr 42 --repo org/repo") — called by dev10x:work-on while executing its 'Request review' plan step
evals.description: GH-1890: no --unattended flag, but an orchestrator calls the skill while executing a plan step with an active task list, which the canonical definition counts as unattended. CI is red, so Step 1.6 refuses without a widget and prints the parseable stop marker.

assertions.text: Does NOT call AskUserQuestion — a plan-step call is unattended
Does NOT invoke dev10x:gh-pr-request-review
Ends the output with the readiness stop marker

evals.name: task-list-without-plan-step-is-attended
evals.description: GH-1890: the supervisor types the command in a session whose task list happens to be open, but no orchestrator is executing a plan step. An active task list alone does not make a run unattended, so the readiness widget fires.

assertions.text: Calls AskUserQuestion with header Readiness before Step 2

evals.name: attended-stop-prints-stop-marker
evals.description: GH-1890: CI is red and the supervisor answers 'Stop — fix it first'. The run ends at Step 1.6 and still prints the same stop marker the sibling prints, so a caller can parse it either way.

assertions.text: Calls AskUserQuestion with header Readiness before stopping
Does NOT invoke dev10x:gh-pr-request-review after the stop answer
Ends the output with the readiness stop marker

evals.name: unattended-delegation-passes-the-flag-verbatim
evals.description: GH-1890: the PR is ready and the run is unattended. Step 2 uses the unattended form: the args carry a bare --unattended, never the bracketed notation.

assertions.text: Invokes dev10x:gh-pr-request-review with --readiness-checked --unattended
Does NOT pass the literal [--unattended]

evals.name: attended-delegation-omits-the-flag
evals.description: GH-1890: the PR is ready and the supervisor invoked the skill directly. Step 2 uses the attended form, so the sibling may still ask its own questions.

assertions.text: Invokes dev10x:gh-pr-request-review with --readiness-checked
Does NOT pass --unattended in any spelling

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should/should-not trigger the request-review skill

should_trigger.query: this PR is ready, ping the team and assign reviewers
should_trigger.rationale: Wants both GitHub assignment and a chat notification — the combined entry point

should_trigger.query: request review on #42 and let the team know in chat
should_trigger.rationale: Explicitly names both halves of this skill's job

should_not_trigger.query: assign @alice as reviewer, no notification needed
should_not_trigger.rationale: GitHub assignment only — use dev10x:gh-pr-request-review directly

should_not_trigger.query: post a message to the team channel about the outage
should_not_trigger.rationale: General chat post, unrelated to a review request — use dev10x:slack or dev10x:gchat

should_not_trigger.query: the PR is still a draft, hold off
